_readme: Vtable layouts for DBSIM.EXE's two class hierarchies -- the simulation objects and the
cockpit widgets -- applied to the Ghidra project by ES2ApplyVtables.java
(tools/ghidra_scripts/). Re-run that script after adding entries here -- it is idempotent.
The widget family is enumerable rather than discovered one class at a time: Borland emitted a
descriptor record per class, stored 12 bytes before that class's vtable, and it carries the
class's own name. tools/scripts/es2_classes.py --vtables walks both directions, so a new
cockpit control's table is looked up from its class name and a table found in the
disassembly is turned back into a class name. Adding a widget class here is therefore a
matter of naming its instance, not of re-deriving the shape.
This is one of three companion files. known_symbols.json owns address->function findings and
known_structs.json owns field layout inside an object. This file owns the SHAPE of a class:
which slot means what, and which addresses hold a table of that shape. A slot's meaning is
recorded once here rather than once per doc that happens to call through it.
Per vtable definition:
name        - Ghidra data-type name, created under category /ES2.
binary      - 'VSHELL' or 'DBSIM' (must match the -process file name at apply time).
description - what the class is; becomes the data type's description.
slots       - ordered, one per 4-byte slot, starting at +0x0 with no gaps. Each has:
name        - the slot's ROLE, not any one class's implementation name.
A slot whose meaning is not established is named
'slot_0xNN' -- never given a guessed role name, so a guess
can never masquerade as a confirmed one (the same rule
known_symbols.json applies to low-confidence functions).
description - evidence and the implementations seen in it.
instances   - the addresses holding a table of this shape. Each has an 'address', a 'label'
naming that particular class's table, and a 'description'.
SLOT COUNT IS A FINDING, NOT A GUESS. A table is followed in memory by whatever the linker
put next, and an over-long definition would type that as function pointers -- a fabrication
that reads as confirmed. A definition's length is established by call sites and by what the
trailing words actually are, and the bytes past it are left undefined. A plausible-looking
code address in the word after the last slot is not evidence: two of the tables here hold a
pointer into a class-descriptor record there, which resolves and disassembles like anything
else. Growing a definition later costs nothing; a wrong one has to be noticed first.
ONE CLASS OF TABLE STATES ITS OWN LENGTH. Where a class has a second base -- the cockpit
widgets and REG_OBJ/TS_REG_OBJ are the cases in DBSIM -- the primary table is followed by two
constants, the second of which is the byte offset from the primary table to the mixin's, so
slot count = (constant - 8) / 4. Check for that pair before reasoning from call sites: it is
the binary saying the length rather than the reader inferring it. Its absence means only that
the class is singly inherited.
NO SIGNATURES. Each slot becomes a function definition with the default (undefined) return and
no declared parameters -- the least the shape can claim. Argument
lists are a separate, per-function finding: record one in known_symbols.json's 'signature'
field, under the rule stated there, not here.

vtables.name: SimObjectVtable
vtables.description: The 34-slot vtable every full simulation object carries -- the base class, the mech class and the flyer class all lay their tables out this way. Its first six slots are ProjectileVtable's, unchanged, so the two hierarchies share a base interface: slots +0x4, +0xc and +0x10 hold the same three functions (0046b801, 004785bf and SimObject_GetShapeRadius) in every table in this file. Slot names are the base class's roles; see the individual instances for what overrides what. The port of this interface is Herculan.Engine.Sim.SimObject.

slots.name: Draw
slots.description: Draw the object. Base installs Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel (004033e4); the mech overrides with Mech_Draw (004174c8).

slots.name: slot_0x04
slots.description: 0046b801 in every table seen -- base, mech, flyer and all four projectile classes. Role not established.

slots.name: Destructor
slots.description: Per-class destructor thunk in the 00427xxx block: base 00427081, mech 00427127, flyer 004271bf. None is a defined function in the database yet.

slots.name: slot_0x0c
slots.description: 004785bf in every table seen. Role not established.

slots.name: GetShapeRadius
slots.description: SimObject_GetShapeRadius (0046b80c) in every table -- reads the radius off the instanced shape rather than any type record. Ported as SimObject.ShapeRadius; see docs/simulation/hit-detection.md.

slots.name: Tick
slots.description: The object's per-tick update. The mech installs Behaviour_DispatchMove (00415afc), which forwards to the current behaviour class rather than moving anything itself; the projectile classes install their own TickUpdate in the same slot.

slots.name: ThinkTick
slots.description: Mech: Behaviour_DispatchThink (00415b38). Second of the three behaviour-class dispatchers; see docs/simulation/ai-dispatch.md.

slots.name: ReassessTick
slots.description: Mech: Behaviour_DispatchReassess (00415b74). Third behaviour-class dispatcher.

slots.name: DirectFireHitTest
slots.description: Hit test AND damage application in one call, offered to each candidate by Sim_RaycastObjectList (00426528). Mech_DirectFireHitTest (00418ba8), Flyer_DirectFireHitTest (00421c8c); the base answers the shared 00496684 stub. See docs/simulation/damage-system.md and hit-detection.md.

slots.name: GetAimNodeTransform
slots.description: The node transform a shot aims at: its +0x14 is the aim point and its +0x1c the sight height. Mech_GetAimNodeTransform (00417b98); base and flyer both install SimObject_GetAimNodeTransform_None (00411a9c), which returns 0 so every caller falls back to the raw origin. See docs/simulation/target-selection.md, 'Aim point'.

slots.name: slot_0x28
slots.description: Base 00411a64, mech 00420ad4, flyer 00411a64. Role not established.

slots.name: HandleCommand
slots.description: Mech_HandleCommand (004157c8). Base and flyer install generic stubs (00411a6c / 004215c0).

slots.name: slot_0x30
slots.description: Base 00411a74, mech 004155c4. Role not established.

slots.name: GetShieldByHeading
slots.description: Given a heading, returns the front or rear shield by which side is within +/-90 degrees. Mech_GetShieldByHeading (004154d0); base and flyer both answer the 00411a4c stub, i.e. zero. Ported as SimObject.ShieldByHeading.

slots.name: GetSpeed
slots.description: How fast the object is travelling, in the units the rest of the simulation quotes distances in. Mech_GetSpeed (00415498). Ported as SimObject.TravelSpeed -- a structure answers zero, which is why the AI leads a shot at a machine and fires straight at a building.

slots.name: GetTorsoTwistAngle
slots.description: The aim offset the sensor and target-selection arcs are measured from, on top of the heading. Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle (00415488); zero for everything else. Ported as SimObject.AimTwist.

slots.name: GetOverallDamage
slots.description: How far gone the object is, as a Q8 fraction: 0 pristine, 256 destroyed. Mech_GetOverallDamage (00415504). Read by the AI's flee check and the mission-order layer's condition tier. Ported as SimObject.OverallDamage.

slots.name: BearingInSensorArc
slots.description: SimObject_BearingInSensorArc (00411acc) in base, mech and flyer alike -- not overridden by any class seen.

slots.name: AiEnemySighted
slots.description: Mech_AiEnemySighted (00412800); base and flyer share 004127f8. Called out of the detection sweep.

slots.name: CompareCombatRating
slots.description: Mech_CompareCombatRating (0041cabc). Base and flyer answer the 00411ac0 stub.

slots.name: AiOnTakingFire
slots.description: Called with (attacker, damage) when something hits this object; applies no damage of its own. Mech_AiOnTakingFire (0041f7b8). Base and flyer install Mech_ShareContact (00411aec), which does the contact-sharing half only. See docs/simulation/ai-targeting.md.

slots.name: ComponentNearestAim
slots.description: Which component a shot or a seeker should aim at. Mech_ComponentNearestAim (0041b534); the rocket seeker calls it through the target to fill its steer point (docs/simulation/rockets.md), and a structure's implementation returns its first surviving component (docs/simulation/ai-weapons.md).

slots.name: ComponentPosition
slots.description: Places the component ComponentNearestAim chose, in world space. Mech_ComponentPosition (0041b60c). Also the per-component position the explosive falloff measures from.

slots.name: GetBodyRadius
slots.description: Mech_GetBodyRadius (00415518) -- the flat 750 of MechTypeRecord.BodyRadius. Ported as SimObject.HitRadius; distinct from GetShapeRadius. See docs/simulation/hit-detection.md, 'The three radius slots'.

slots.name: OnTargetNeutralised
slots.description: Base 00411b2c is an empty stub; mech 00415710 is Mech_CreditNeutralisedTarget. Called on the ATTACKER by Mech_ComponentDamageWrite when its victim goes out of the fight, carrying the victim and the victim's immobilised reading from before the change -- kill credit and the two squad callouts. See docs/simulation/component-damage.md.

slots.name: AiOnLineOfFireBlocked
slots.description: Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked (0041dd2c): copies the machine's current target position to mech+0x31e and sets mech+0xad. Called from the tail of Sim_RaycastObjectList. See docs/simulation/ai-combat-states.md.

slots.name: SetRunInto
slots.description: SimObject_SetRunInto (0042200c) in all eight instances, with no override: obj+0xb1 = 1, "something ran into me". Two callers, both collision sweeps naming whatever blocked a move -- Mech_CollisionTest and FUN_0046a510, the sweep in StructureGroundVehicleVtable's tick slot. Mech_BehaviourRamTick is the only reader and nothing clears the byte.

slots.name: MissileLockState
slots.description: Mech_MissileLockState (004155ac): returns the per-missile-subtype LOCK flag, NOT an ammunition count. Rocket_Fire will not attach a target without it. See known_symbols.json's entry for 004155ac.

slots.name: ApplyExplosiveDamage
slots.description: What an explosion does to this object, called on every object the blast sweep finds in range. Mech_ApplyExplosiveDamage (004187d0); base and flyer share SimObject_ApplyExplosiveDamage (00411b3c). See docs/simulation/damage-system.md, 'Explosive damage'.

slots.name: ComponentDamageWrite
slots.description: The shared component-health write every damage path funnels into. Mech_ComponentDamageWrite (00417de4), Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite (00421bb4); both of the mech's death branches fire the object's defeat action from here. The base answers the 00496684 stub.

slots.name: ApplyFormationOffset
slots.description: Places a group member at its formation offset from the leader. Mech_ApplyFormationOffset (00417898); run over every non-leader member by Group_DeploymentCheck for the walk-on arrival verbs. See docs/simulation/mission-deployment.md.

slots.name: GetCollisionRadius
slots.description: The radius at which this object blocks a walking machine; zero means walk through me. Mech_GetCollisionRadius (0041552c). Ported as SimObject.CollisionRadius.

slots.name: NextTargetableComponent
slots.description: (this, cursor, int *componentId) -- step a targeting-pod component lock to the next component this object still has, answering the new cursor and writing the component id out. Mech_NextTargetableComponent (00415558) walks a fixed seven-slot rotation, Base_NextTargetableComponent (00403624) walks the structure type's whole component list, and the base class answers -1. The targeting pod is the only caller; see docs/simulation/target-selection.md.

slots.name: ComponentPresent
slots.description: (this, componentId) -- whether this object still has that component, from its occupancy array. Mech_ComponentPresent (00415540), Base_ComponentPresent (0040360c); the base class answers 1 for anything. Asked only by the targeting pod, to notice that the component it had locked has been shot off. See docs/simulation/target-selection.md.

instances.label: SimObjectBaseVtable
instances.description: The base class's own table, installed first by Mech_Constructor (00415bb0) at 00415bf4 before the mech's own replaces it at 00415c60. Most slots hold generic 00411axx stubs; the shared 00496684 stands in for the ones a bare object cannot answer.

instances.label: MechVtable
instances.description: The HERC class. Installed by Mech_Constructor (00415bb0) at 00415c60, after the base table. Overrides 26 of the 34 slots; the table ends at +0x88, where a data block of literals begins.

instances.label: FlyerVtable
instances.description: The flyer class. Installed by Flyer_Constructor (004215f4) at 00421624, after the base table. Same 34-slot shape as the base; it is a sibling of the mech rather than a subset -- its objects come from a different pool and are 0x291 bytes to the mech's 0x36a.

instances.label: StructureVtable
instances.description: The structure base class, and the concrete class for a plain building: BASES.DAT types 0-4, 7, 9, 0x0c-0x1c, 0x1f, 0x21 and 0x24-0x2c. Base_Construct (00405314) installs it FIRST in every one of its five branches and the other four tables then overwrite it, so those four are derived from this one. Its +0x3c returns the shared 00411a5c zero stub -- a plain building has no aim angle -- and Base_Construct sets disarmed (+0xa5) on it at spawn.

instances.label: StructureRadarVtable
instances.description: BASES.DAT types 5, 6, 0x1d and 0x1e. Derived from StructureVtable, and the only slot it overrides is the destructor -- its think and its aim angle are the plain building's. What makes it a radar mast is the construction, not the table: Base_Construct latches scannerActive (+0x96) on, and disarmed (+0xa5) with it.

instances.label: StructureArmedVtable
instances.description: BASES.DAT types 8, 0x0b, 0x20 and 0x23, and the parent of StructureGroundVehicleVtable. Derived from StructureVtable. THIS IS THE CLASS THAT AIMS: it replaces the +0x3c zero stub with Base_GetTurretAngle (00403594), which returns the structure's own angle at +0x20f, and its think (FUN_00404100) maintains the selected-target refcount at +0x1a2. Base_Construct does not set disarmed on it, which is the same conclusion reached from the other direction.

instances.label: StructureGroundVehicleVtable
instances.description: BASES.DAT types 0x2d-0x3d, the types Base_Construct classifies as targetClass 3 and gives a hit radius of 10 rather than 5. Derived from StructureArmedVtable -- Base_Construct installs StructureVtable, then StructureArmedVtable, then this -- so it inherits the turret angle and overrides only the destructor and the think (FUN_0046a5d0).

instances.label: StructureType0x22Vtable
instances.description: BASES.DAT type 0x22 alone. Derived from StructureVtable, overriding the destructor and the think (FUN_004045c8), which latches disarmed (+0xa5) once every one of the type's components has been destroyed -- so this class starts armed and can lose it, where a plain building is born disarmed. It does not override the aim angle. The role of the type is not established; the label names the type index rather than guessing one.

vtables.name: ProjectileVtable
vtables.description: The six-slot table the projectile classes carry, and the interface SimObjectVtable's first six slots extend -- which is what lets the draw pass and the raycast walk a projectile and a machine the same way. SIX IS ESTABLISHED, not a floor, on four independent grounds. (1) No code in the class family's own region (0040a100-0040c500: all five constructors, destructors, tick and draw functions) calls any slot above +0x14 on itself. (2) The six CALL dword ptr [reg + 0x18] sites in that region are all the same deleting-destructor call on the MEMBER object at this+0x34, under a null check and with the flag argument 3 -- Bullet_Construct's destructor at 0040b6af and the base's at 0040c38d are byte-for-byte the same sequence -- so +0x18 belongs to that member's class, not this one. (3) The word after +0x14 is not a code pointer in two of the five tables: 00000001 in the bullet's, 00000000 in the beam tracer's. (4) Where it does look like one it is descriptor data -- the base's 0040c3d8 sits inside a class-descriptor record next to the string 'BEAM *', and the rocket's 0046b7c8 at the head of one whose name string is 'TSShapeInstance'; neither address has a function prologue and neither is reached by any call. The class 004a0b98, which the projectile base derives from, independently shows the same six slots followed by two null words before the next table begins.

slots.name: Draw
slots.description: Bullet_Draw (0040a120) for the launcher round and the gun round alike; BeamTracer_Draw (0040bc14) for the beam class. See docs/simulation/beam-visuals.md.

slots.name: slot_0x04
slots.description: 0046b801, the same value SimObjectVtable's +0x04 holds. Role not established.

slots.name: Destructor
slots.description: The deleting destructor: Rocket_Dtor (0040ab8d), Bullet_Dtor (0040b64d), BeamTracer_Dtor (0040ba94), Grenade_Dtor (0040ad2c), ProjectileBase_Dtor (0040c324), ProjectileSuperBase_Dtor (0046b890). Takes a flags argument whose low bit asks it to free the object, which it does through 0047743c.

slots.name: slot_0x0c
slots.description: 004785bf, as in SimObjectVtable. Role not established.

slots.name: GetShapeRadius
slots.description: SimObject_GetShapeRadius (0046b80c), shared with the full simulation objects.

slots.name: Tick
slots.description: Rocket_TickUpdate (0040a538), Bullet_TickUpdate (0040b124), BeamTracer_LifeTick (0040c2a0). The base answers the 00496684 stub. See docs/simulation/rockets.md and projectiles.md.

instances.label: ProjectileSuperBaseVtable
instances.description: The class the projectile base derives from: its destructor (0040c324) installs this table at 0040c353 after restoring its own, which is the ordinary base-before-teardown sequence. Six slots, then two null words before the next table of the same shape at 004a0bb8. Which class it is has not been established -- the 0046bxxx block its slots point into is shared engine code, and SimObject_GetShapeRadius (0046b80c) at +0x10 is the same function every table in this file holds there.

instances.label: ProjectileBaseVtable
instances.description: The projectile base class's own table, installed first by both Missile_Construct (0040a948, at 0040a97a) and Bullet_Construct (0040af6c, at 0040af9e) before each derived table replaces it.

instances.label: RocketVtable
instances.description: The launcher round -- PROJ.DAT Type 0, 14-byte type table out of ROCKETS.DAT. Installed by Missile_Construct (0040a948) at 0040a99c. See docs/simulation/rockets.md.

instances.label: BulletVtable
instances.description: The travelling gun round -- PROJ.DAT Type 2, own 14-byte type table out of BULLETS.DAT. Installed by Bullet_Construct (0040af6c) at 0040afbe. See docs/simulation/projectiles.md.

instances.label: BeamTracerVtable
instances.description: The beam tracer -- PROJ.DAT Type 3, both the straight beam and the jagged ELF/ELF2 chain. See docs/simulation/beam-visuals.md.

instances.label: GrenadeVtable
instances.description: DEAD CODE. The Type-3 constructor that builds against this table is never called, and its Tick slot is FUN_0040acb4 (return 0), so an instance would never move or die. Retail Type-3 records are unreachable data -- see known_symbols.json's entry for that constructor. Typed here so the table is not mistaken for a live class later.

vtables.name: CockpitWidgetVtable
vtables.description: The seven-slot table every clickable cockpit widget on the CTLButtonControl branch carries, at object +0x17 -- the offset the class's own Borland descriptor record states, so a widget's primary vtable is always reached the same way. SEVEN IS ESTABLISHED, and on a concrete class the block states it outright: the second of the two constants after the table is the byte offset of the mixin's vtable from the start of the primary one, so slot count = (constant - 8) / 4, and every button class carries 0x24. The three input functions that call through the table fix the slot numbers independently (Widget_OnMouseUp (00452870) reads +0x10 then calls +0x08, Widget_OnMouseDown (004527a0) calls +0x18, Widget_Repaint (00452a90) calls +0x04), and the word at +0x1c is not an eighth slot -- in every table on this branch it is either the next class's descriptor pointer (the [descriptor][0][0][vtable] block header this linker emits), the first of the two constants, or padding. Four of those next-class pointers disassemble as code and would read as a confirmed slot. The slider branch is a separate shape with a genuine +0x1c; see CockpitSliderWidgetVtable. Each class's table is found from its name, and each address here from its table, by tools/scripts/es2_classes.py --vtables, which reads the descriptor record stored 12 bytes before every table. See docs/formats/cockpit-input.md.

slots.name: Paint
slots.description: Redraw the widget's own content -- re-resolve its caption, pick its frame and colour. Called by slot +0x0c's stage 2, never directly by the input layer. CTLControl's table holds the empty 00452ab2; CTLButtonControl installs 00455545.

slots.name: Invalidate
slots.description: Widget_Repaint (00452a90) calls this and nothing else, so no widget paints inside its own click. The PanelSelectGadget branch installs Widget_InvalidateDeferred (00455524), whose whole body is this->[0x1f] = 2; CTLControl's default (00452ab7) is empty.

slots.name: OnClick
slots.description: (this, value) -- commit the click, with slot +0x10's value. Called by Widget_OnMouseUp (00452870). Most leaves inherit Widget_ForwardClickToOwner (00438e3c) from PanelSelectGadget, which calls owner->vtable[0] through the owner pointer at this+0x24; the MFD's latching class, HDDSelectGadget and the throttle override it.

slots.name: FlushDeferredPaint
slots.description: Run once a frame down the widget tree: at this->[0x1f] == 2 calls slot 0 and decrements, at 1 calls Widget_DrawToCockpit (0043122c) and decrements. CTLControl's default (0045554a) is empty.

slots.name: GetValue
slots.description: The value slot +0x08 is handed. Widget_GetButtonValue (00455530) returns the global mouse-button word 0049db6c, i.e. WHICH BUTTON clicked -- 1 for left, 2 for right. Read by Widget_OnMouseUp immediately before it calls +0x08.

slots.name: SetValue
slots.description: (this, value). CTLControl's default (0045553b) is empty; the slider family overrides it.

slots.name: DragMove
slots.description: (this, x, y) -- the pointer moved while this widget holds the mouse capture. Widget_OnMouseDown (004527a0) calls it the moment it begins a capture, and CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue calls it for every move until the release. CTLControl's default (00455540) is empty; only the sliders implement it.

instances.label: CTLControlVtable
instances.description: The root of the shape: every slot is an empty stub, and the table is followed by neither a mixin table nor the two subobject constants. Not instantiated in the cockpit -- it exists to be inherited from.

instances.label: CTLButtonControlVtable
instances.description: The clickable base every cockpit gadget derives from; 0x20 bytes by its descriptor record. Overrides +0x00 (00455545) and +0x04 (00455559) only. No PanelGadget subobject of its own, so no mixin table follows it.

instances.label: PanelSelectGadgetVtable
instances.description: The momentary-button class, 0x40 bytes: CTLButtonControl plus a PanelGadget mixin at +0x20. It is here that +0x08 becomes Widget_ForwardClickToOwner (00438e3c) and +0x04 becomes Widget_InvalidateDeferred (00455524), which is why most leaves need to override neither.

instances.label: PanelStateGadgetVtable
instances.description: The latching-button class, derived from PanelSelectGadget. Overrides +0x0c with 0044c0b0; its +0x08 is still the forwarder.

instances.label: PanelListGadgetVtable
instances.description: The click-region class -- a rectangle that reports where in itself it was hit rather than acting as a button. Overrides +0x00 and +0x04 (00450565 / 0045055b), and its mixin's OnClick thunk is the 00496684 stub.

instances.label: SystemGadgetVtable
instances.description: A console button, 0x60 bytes, built in pairs by maybe_SysButtonPair_Ctor; see SystemGadget_Ctor (00434664).

instances.label: ScrollTriggerVtable
instances.description: The manual's screen-edge view change: 0x24 bytes, derived from CTLButtonControl, overriding +0x04 (00455559) and +0x08 (ScrollTrigger_OnClick, 00434df0). Three are built by CockpitView_BuildScrollTriggers (00433770) as strips along the bottom, left and right edges of the display, and a click on one calls CockpitView_HandleEdgeTrigger. No PanelGadget subobject: the block ends at +0x1c with linker padding, so +0x20 is a plain owner pointer and the strip is silent.

instances.label: HUDRovingGunsightGadgetVtable
instances.description: The click surface over the 3D view, built by Gunsight_ClickSurface_Ctor (0043c120); see docs/formats/hud-target-indicator.md. No PanelGadget subobject, so it is silent.

instances.label: WeaponRangeSelectGadgetVtable
instances.description: The weapon-range gauge's button; WeaponRangeSelectGadget_Ctor (00442c00).

instances.label: ChainedWeaponSelectGadgetVtable
instances.description: A weapon row, from EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor and AmmoWeaponGauge_Ctor; see docs/simulation/weapon-mounts.md.

instances.label: WeaponSelectGadgetVtable
instances.description: A pod row -- the weapon-row class without chain membership, built only by PodGauge_Ctor; see docs/simulation/equipment-pods.md.

instances.label: ShieldsSelectGadgetVtable
instances.description: A shield facing, built by ShieldsGauge_FacingCtor (00444aec). Overrides +0x00 with ShieldFacing_Paint (00444b5c) and +0x0c with ShieldFacing_FlushDeferredPaint (00444b70), which blits without rebuilding content. Its owner is the ShieldsGauge, whose own four-slot table at 0049ca1d is a different shape and is not in the clickable list.

instances.label: MFDListGadgetVtable
instances.description: The MFD's screen-content click region; MFDListGadget_Ctor (004475d4).

instances.label: MFDStateGadgetVtable
instances.description: An MFD latching button; MFDStateGadget_Ctor (0044741c). See docs/formats/mfd.md.

instances.label: MFDSelectGadgetVtable
instances.description: An MFD momentary button; MFDSelectGadget_Ctor (004472e4).

instances.label: HDDisplayGadgetVtable
instances.description: 0x24 bytes, derived straight from CTLButtonControl; HDDisplayGadget_Ctor (0044be94) installs it at 0044beb5, its only store. Its first three slots are the 00496684 stub. No PanelGadget subobject, so it is silent.

instances.label: HDDSelectGadgetVtable
instances.description: A Heads-Down Display button; HddButton_Ctor (0044baac). See docs/formats/heads-down-display.md.

instances.label: HDDListGadgetVtable
instances.description: The command screen's order lists; HDDListGadget_Ctor (0044f650).

instances.label: HDDMapGadgetVtable
instances.description: The F7 map's clickable surface; HddMarker_Ctor (0044f130). Overrides the first four slots. No PanelGadget subobject, so it is silent.

instances.label: AlertSelectGadgetVtable
instances.description: An alert-panel option row; PanelButton_Ctor (00454f64). See docs/simulation/preferences.md.

vtables.name: CockpitSliderWidgetVtable
vtables.description: The eight-slot table the CTLSliderControl branch carries at object +0x17: CockpitWidgetVtable's seven slots with the same roles and the same call sites, plus +0x1c. The extra slot is present from CTLSliderControl down and absent from every button class, which is the one place the family's shape is not uniform. EIGHT IS ESTABLISHED the same way as seven: a concrete slider's second constant is 0x28, i.e. (0x28 - 8) / 4 = 8 slots, and the word at +0x20 is the subobject-offset constant 0x3e on a concrete slider and the next class's descriptor pointer on an abstract one, never a code address. See docs/formats/cockpit-input.md.

slots.name: Paint
slots.description: Redraw the widget's own content -- re-resolve its caption, pick its frame and colour. Called by slot +0x0c's stage 2, never directly by the input layer. CTLControl's table holds the empty 00452ab2; CTLButtonControl installs 00455545.

slots.name: Invalidate
slots.description: Widget_Repaint (00452a90) calls this and nothing else, so no widget paints inside its own click. The PanelSelectGadget branch installs Widget_InvalidateDeferred (00455524), whose whole body is this->[0x1f] = 2; CTLControl's default (00452ab7) is empty.

slots.name: OnClick
slots.description: (this, value) -- commit the click, with slot +0x10's value. Called by Widget_OnMouseUp (00452870). Most leaves inherit Widget_ForwardClickToOwner (00438e3c) from PanelSelectGadget, which calls owner->vtable[0] through the owner pointer at this+0x24; the MFD's latching class, HDDSelectGadget and the throttle override it.

slots.name: FlushDeferredPaint
slots.description: Run once a frame down the widget tree: at this->[0x1f] == 2 calls slot 0 and decrements, at 1 calls Widget_DrawToCockpit (0043122c) and decrements. CTLControl's default (0045554a) is empty.

slots.name: GetValue
slots.description: The value slot +0x08 is handed. Widget_GetButtonValue (00455530) returns the global mouse-button word 0049db6c, i.e. WHICH BUTTON clicked -- 1 for left, 2 for right. Read by Widget_OnMouseUp immediately before it calls +0x08.

slots.name: SetValue
slots.description: (this, value). CTLControl's default (0045553b) is empty; the slider family overrides it.

slots.name: DragMove
slots.description: (this, x, y) -- the pointer moved while this widget holds the mouse capture. Widget_OnMouseDown (004527a0) calls it the moment it begins a capture, and CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue calls it for every move until the release. CTLControl's default (00455540) is empty; only the sliders implement it.

slots.name: RecomputeScale
slots.description: Recompute the mapping between the widget's rect and its value range. Present only on the CTLSliderControl branch -- the button branch's table stops at +0x18, and the word at +0x1c there is the next class's descriptor pointer. CTLSliderControl installs the 00496684 stub; CTLHSlider and CTLVSlider install axis-specific implementations (004525a8 / 00452694).

instances.label: CTLSliderControlVtable
instances.description: The slider branch's base, 0x3e bytes, derived from CTLControl rather than from CTLButtonControl -- which is why a slider is not a button and carries the other mixin. Adds +0x1c, holding the 00496684 stub here. No mixin table follows it.

instances.label: CTLHSliderVtable
instances.description: The horizontal slider base. Installs the x-axis implementations in +0x10, +0x14, +0x18 and +0x1c (00452544, 0045255c, 004524f8, 004525a8), which is where a slider's real value and its drag come from.

instances.label: CTLVSliderVtable
instances.description: The vertical slider base, the y-axis twin of CTLHSlider (00452628, 00452644, 004525d8, 00452694).

instances.label: PanelHSliderGadgetVtable
instances.description: CTLHSlider plus a PanelSliderGadget mixin at +0x3e, 0x7e bytes. Overrides +0x0c with 0045578e.

instances.label: PanelVSliderGadgetVtable
instances.description: The vertical twin; +0x0c is 00448c02.

instances.label: ThrottleVSliderGadgetVtable
instances.description: The throttle slider every one of the nine retail .GAU files uses; ThrottleSlider_CtorV (00447e24). Overrides +0x00 through +0x0c. See docs/formats/cockpit-input.md.

instances.label: WeaponSliderGadgetVtable

vtables.name: PanelGadgetMixinVtable
vtables.description: The four-slot table of the PanelGadget mixin -- the second base every concrete cockpit widget carries alongside CTLButtonControl or CTLHSlider/CTLVSlider, and the reason a widget has two vtable pointers. The descriptor records name it: PanelGadget is 8 bytes with its vptr at +0x00, PanelSliderGadget derives from it, and the subobject constant that precedes each table (0x20 for a button, 0x3e for a slider) is where that base sits inside the object -- exactly the amount the table's adjustor thunks subtract. THE MIXIN ADDS NO BEHAVIOUR of its own: three of the four slots thunk straight back into the primary table, and the fourth is the console click. It is not a second interface to implement but the single switch that decides whether a control makes a sound. A class with no mixin table -- CTLControl, CTLButtonControl, CTLSliderControl, CTLHSlider, CTLVSlider, ScrollTrigger, HDDisplayGadget, HDDMapGadget and HUDRovingGunsightGadget -- is silent for want of the base, not for want of an override. The block layout is [descriptor ptr][0][0][primary vtable][subobject offset][mixin vtable offset][this table], and the second constant is that last offset: the distance in bytes from the start of the primary vtable to this one, 0x24 for a button (7 slots * 4 + 8) against 0x28 for a slider (8 * 4 + 8). It holds in all 22 blocks in DBSIM that carry the pair, the two outside the widget family included -- REG_OBJ and TS_REG_OBJ declare a mixin at +0x0c with the constant 0x1c, which is the same arithmetic over a five-slot primary table. The pair is declared by whichever class first mixes the second base in and inherited unchanged by everything below it, so it varies with the branch and not with the leaf. VSHELL's own CTL family carries no such pair anywhere: its widgets are singly inherited and have no mixin. See docs/formats/cockpit-input.md.

slots.name: Paint
slots.description: Adjustor thunk onto the primary table's +0x00: ADD dword ptr [ESP+4], -<subobject offset>; JMP <primary implementation>. The two abstract mixin tables hold the 00496684 stub instead.

slots.name: FlushDeferredPaint
slots.description: Adjustor thunk onto the primary table's +0x0c.

slots.name: ClickSound
slots.description: Widget_ClickSound (00438e2c) in PanelGadget's table and in every class that derives from it -- push 0x11; call Sound_Play, ignoring the pointer it is handed. PanelSliderGadget replaces it with 00439014, an empty stub, and every slider inherits that. A widget therefore clicks or stays silent according to which of the two mixins it carries, and a class with no mixin at all makes no sound. See docs/formats/audio.md.

slots.name: OnClick
slots.description: Adjustor thunk onto the primary table's +0x08.

instances.label: PanelGadgetVtable
instances.description: The mixin's own table, and the one place the console click is declared: three 00496684 stubs around Widget_ClickSound (00438e2c) at +0x08. The class is 8 bytes and its descriptor puts its vptr at +0x00, not at +0x17.

instances.label: PanelSliderGadgetVtable
instances.description: The slider mixin, derived from PanelGadget. Its one change is +0x08, replaced with the empty 00439014 -- which is the whole of why a slider is silent and a button is not.
